🎖️ Five of these Hollywood stars served in World War II. One never did.

And here's a twist: one of them refused to carry a gun… and went anyway.

Can you spot the impostor? 👇 https://t.co/8bSJSBsdIi
⏰ 3 hours left and it's neck and neck! Bradys, Cleavers and Waltons are all within 2 points. Your vote could decide it! 🏡

🤠 Ben Johnson is the only person in history to win a world rodeo championship AND an Academy Award.

He was a real cowboy, the son of an Oklahoma rancher. In the early 1940s he came to Hollywood delivering a load of horses for a movie, and Howard Hughes hired him as a horse https://t.co/y00W3rw13h

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 America's favorite TV dad couldn't stand his own show.

Robert Reed played Mike Brady, but he'd studied Shakespeare at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London. He expected serious acting. Instead, he got Marcia getting hit with a football.

He fought the writers over plots https://t.co/AZOHMFzHUI

Fun fact: The Brady house is real. It's in Studio City, California, and HGTV bought it in 2018 for $3.5 million so the Brady kids could help restore it. 🏠

Tell me who I left out 👇
🏡 Which classic TV family would you most want living next door?

Boyd also cleaned up the character. In the original books, Hoppy was a rough-talking, hard-drinking cowhand.

Boyd's Hoppy never shot first, never killed the bad guy and drank sarsaparilla. Boyd said that since parents trusted Hoppy, he had to live up to it. 🐴

So far you've said: The Exorcist, Jaws, Salem's Lot (that kid at the window!) and The Crawling Hand. 😱

Fun fact: House on Haunted Hill is now in the public domain, so you can watch it free tonight if you dare. 👻

Keep 'em coming 👇

🤠 In 1948, William Boyd bet everything he owned on a gamble nobody else in Hollywood would take.

He'd played Hopalong Cassidy in 66 movies, and he believed this new thing called television would want them.

So he bought the TV rights to Hoppy and all his films for $350,000. https://t.co/6aJBBwZCEf

😂 Tim Conway wasn't supposed to be "Tim."

He was born Thomas Conway in Ohio in 1933. After two years in the Army (1956–58), he landed a job writing promos at a Cleveland TV station.

Then actress Rose Marie, Sally from The Dick Van Dyke Show, saw him in Cleveland and told Steve https://t.co/dJRQgefK0O
